- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates, especially in mid-to-late horizon; increase forecast values slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 1.97→2.31), suggesting overreaction to sentiment-driven momentum; apply dampening factor to 3rd–5th day forecasts post-spike.
- Mean reversion is evident: forecasts often drift toward historical mean (e.g., 1.8–1.9 range) after 10–15 days; adjust later horizon forecasts toward recent 7–14 day average.
- Sentiment volatility correlates with forecast error: high sentiment volatility → higher forecast error; smooth forecasts using sentiment moving average (3-day) for volatile sentiment periods.
- Horizon-specific: 1–3 day forecasts are often too optimistic; 15–30 day forecasts are too pessimistic unless sentiment is strongly bullish; adjust based on sentiment trend direction.
